subject: Red gate / red landing repairs itself by default: budget = D-050 ② (3 repair rounds after the first red, one config key), and unattributed red / environment-suspect get one bounded diagnosis round instead of a page
objective: Fill the three gaps left after the inventory below: (1) the repair budget reads one key `repair.max_rounds` (default 3 = repair rounds after the first red, D-050 ②) through one function, replacing the two `retry_limit or 2` copies in auto-fix.sh and ticket.py's own; (2) an unattributed red (rc != 0, failures []) dispatches ONE diagnosis round inside the same budget instead of paging main; (3) an environment-suspect gate (rc 86) is re-run once mechanically and, if still 86, gets ONE diagnosis round; a second consecutive unattributed / 86 outcome pages main. Single-ticket gate, single-ticket land and batch land share the contract. Ordinary technical failures no longer reach main (D-049 ③).
acceptance: A1 One budget key: board/config.json `repair: {"max_rounds": 3, "env_rerun": 1}` (project_config.py knows both keys with these defaults; `actl doctor` on a config without them reports nothing wrong). `ticket.py create` writes `retry_limit` = repair.max_rounds at creation (3 when the key is absent) instead of the literal 2; a ticket's explicit `retry_limit` wins over config (per-ticket override, as today). The limit is computed by ONE function in ticket.py (`repair_limit(ticket, conf)` -> rounds allowed = retry_limit + 1 when the ticket has a number, else max_rounds + 1); auto-fix.sh obtains it through `ticket.py` (a subcommand or the status reader), the two heredoc copies are gone (no `retry_limit") or 2` arithmetic left in scripts/auto-fix.sh: grep `or 2) + 1` = 0 hits; comments may still mention the field). A's board/config.json: add `repair`, remove `batch_fix.rounds` so the batch budget also comes from max_rounds (batch_fix.rounds, when present, still wins for projects that set it; A does not).

A2 Budget semantics (D-050 ②): with max_rounds 3 and a ticket without retry_limit, a gate red on rounds 1..4 dispatches worker rounds 2, 3, 4 and after round 4's red the ticket is Blocked/owner=main with one decision page; with ticket retry_limit 1 only round 2 is dispatched. A diagnosis round (A3/A4) counts as one of those rounds. A model switch inside a round (quota -> next candidate) and the mechanical env re-run (A4) do not count (existing #121/#131 tests pin the former). A new auto-fix process (new pid, same ticket) continues at the next round number, never restarts at 2 (status files are the truth; already true - pinned by a test).

A3 Unattributed red: status rc != 0, failures [] and no hard-block note -> auto-fix dispatches a diagnosis round: the dispatch file has `## 診斷` (gate rc, status state, the last 200 lines of the gate log, the gate command to re-run, the rules: find why no attributable red list was produced; allowed fixes are harness / test-infrastructure / in-repo environment setup; never weaken or skip tests; if the cause is outside the repo write `OBJECTION: blocking <cause>` and hand in nothing) and no red list; `ticket.attempt.start` carries kv round_kind=diagnosis and diagnosis=unattributed (A4's diagnosis round: diagnosis=env); the round is received, gated and reviewed like any other. Afterwards: attributable red -> normal repair continues; green -> normal green path; unattributed again -> rc 4 and ONE page saying 'diagnosis round r did not make the red attributable' (no second consecutive diagnosis). Batch: the same section in reports/batch/<stamp>/dispatch-round<r>.md when the batch red is unattributed; after a second unattributed outcome the suspect-kicking step is skipped (no red list to match) and one page is written.

A4 Environment suspect: gate.sh with auto-fix on and rc 86 calls auto-fix (the '環境可疑,不自動派' refusal is removed; `--no-auto-fix` keeps today's page and no dispatch). auto-fix on a status whose state is env_suspect (or environment_suspect rows non-empty): first re-runs the same gate command once (`repair.env_rerun`, default 1; event `gate.rerun` kv reason=env_suspect; not a round); rc 0 -> green path; rc 1 attributable -> normal repair; rc 86 / unattributed again -> ONE diagnosis round whose `## 診斷` section also lists the environment_suspect rows (source, engine, why, count, threshold) and the preflight output; if that round's gate is 86 / unattributed again -> one page 'environment: needs a human' and stop. A typed `auto-fix.sh <n>` over an env suspect keeps printing the existing warning line (test pinned) and then follows the same path. land.sh: the full suite's rc 86 is told apart from 1 (land.fail note names env_suspect; status state env_suspect) before auto_fix_all / batch_fix, which then follow A4 instead of reading an empty red list as 'unattributed'.

A5 Pages to main only at: budget exhausted (A2), second consecutive unattributed / 86 (A3/A4), worker objection escalate, hard_block hit, guard violation, candidates exhausted - each scenario in the harness ends with exactly one decision page; green rounds and diagnosis rounds that lead to an attributable red write events only (D-032).

A6 Mechanical stops unchanged and never diagnosed: hard_block hit (mechanical_stop), rc 8 guard, rc 7 candidates exhausted, rc 3 objection, rc 5 no hand-in keep their rc, page and state (existing tests pin them).

A7 docs: docs/WORKFLOW.md '回歸紅了之後' names `repair.max_rounds` / `repair.env_rerun`, the diagnosis round and the one-consecutive bound; docs/DESIGN-ENV-SUSPECT.md 理由 5 gets a dated note that D-076 replaces 'never dispatch over env suspect' with 'one re-run, then one diagnosis round' (gate's behaviour change); tickets/SCHEMA.md retry_limit row says where the default comes from.
in_scope: repair budget key + single reader; diagnosis round dispatch section for unattributed red and env suspect (single ticket and batch); gate.sh / land.sh hand-off to auto-fix on rc 86; pages only at the listed terminal states; docs.
out_of_scope: No change to flake rerun, regression-red tickets, suspect-kicking rules, scheduler reland_max, review flow, candidate chains; no Controller (#120 cancelled); no driver-death handling (#117); no new agent kind or prompt route; docs/DECISIONS.md and docs/VISION.md (hard_block).

verify.notes: #125 cases are the T125* classes at the end of the five modules (29 cases; 24 red on base, 5 green guards of kept behaviour). auto-fix cases script the per-round gate through gate.rerun_cmd (fake gate writes status via scripts/status.py, plan in gate-script.json); land cases stub gate.sh/auto-fix.sh. Diagnosis kv: the case accepts any field of round 2's ticket.attempt.start row whose value is 'diagnosis' (a kv literally named kind crashes event.py, see objection). Page wording is matched loosely (第 2 輪|round 2; 環境|environment). baseline.candidate holds the round copy path because red ran with a scratch control root (AC_ROOT) - the copy is deleted after hand-in.

interface_contracts.config: board/config.json `repair`: {max_rounds: int >= 0 (repair rounds after the first red; default 3), env_rerun: int >= 0 (mechanical gate re-runs on rc 86; default 1)}; `batch_fix.rounds` optional override for batches; ticket `retry_limit` optional per-ticket override (null/absent = config).
interface_contracts.dispatch: a diagnosis round's dispatch file has the section header `## 診斷` in place of the red-list section; `ticket.attempt.start` kv round_kind=diagnosis plus diagnosis=unattributed|env (not kv `kind`: an event row's `kind` is the event type and `event.py emit --kv kind=...` raises TypeError - triage #125 r1); the EVIDENCE / result block, apply, gate and review are unchanged.

Already done: attributable gate red -> auto-fix next round with the red list, limit `retry_limit+1` rounds (ticket.py cmd_round; auto-fix.sh:575 and :2146 each recompute `int(retry_limit or 2)+1`), retry_limit written as 2 by `ticket.py create` -> first red + 2 repairs, while D-050 ② says 3 repairs after the first red; single-ticket land full-suite red -> auto_fix_all -> the same budget (land.sh:329); batch land red -> batch_fix up to `batch_fix.rounds` (config: 2) then suspect-kicking and one re-land (land.sh:684); scheduler re-lands only on a new gated head, <= schedule.reland_max 2, and stops on any auto-fix rc != 0 (schedule.py); round numbers persist across restarts (status files + ticket.repair_round) and a model switch re-runs the same round (#121/#131) - so 'does not reset on restart / model change' already holds; hard_block hit is mechanical_stop (auto-fix.sh:613); flake rerun and regression-red tickets exist. Gaps: G1 budget is 2 not 3 and lives in three places; G2 unattributed red -> rc 4 + decision page, no worker (auto-fix.sh:1130; batch 2796/3044); G3 gate rc 86 -> gate.sh:546-556 refuses to call auto-fix and pages ('先修環境'), a typed auto-fix warns and goes (auto-fix.sh:1116) - at land, the full suite's 86 is not told apart from red (land.sh has 0 hits for env_suspect) and ends as 'unattributed' rc 4. Evidence of the cost: the container's full suite has died with rc 137 inside a worker round (reports/t169 worker log last tool result 'Exit code 137'), and every such stop today is a page for main.
hypotheses:
H1 The budget is one number: repair rounds after the first red, for gate and land alike (D-050 ② original wording: 首次紅後最多 3 次修補). Falsify: a place where a 'round' is not a worker dispatch (flake rerun, mechanical env re-run) - those are not counted (acceptance A4 pins the mechanical re-run as free).
H2 A diagnosis round can be the ordinary worker dispatch with a different section (`## 診斷`: rc, state, suspect rows, log tail, preflight output, gate command) instead of the red list, so no new agent kind, prompt route or receiving path is needed (same apply/gate/review afterwards). Falsify: the dispatch builder requires failures[] non-empty somewhere - then that guard moves to 'failures[] non-empty OR diagnosis'.
H3 One consecutive diagnosis round is enough bound: if the agent could not make the red attributable, a second blind round would only burn tokens (D-019 reason 5's asymmetry). Falsify: none planned; the bound is a decision, see outline.
H4 Re-running the gate once on 86 is cheaper than a page: a page costs a main turn (context resend) plus a human; a re-run costs wall time only. Falsify: the second run is also 86 every time in practice - then env_rerun=0 in config turns it off without code change.

objections.body: interface_contracts.dispatch says ticket.attempt.start carries kv kind=diagnosis, but event.py rows already use kind for the event type and `--kv kind=...` crashes emit (TypeError, measured); implemented as kv round_kind=diagnosis (plus diagnosis=env|unattributed) — the ticket's kv name should read round_kind so the verifier's cases match.

triage.reason: ticket-wrong confirmed - `event.py emit --kv kind=diagnosis` raises TypeError (emit(kind, **fields) collides; reproduced by opener on an empty AC_ROOT), so the kv is renamed to round_kind=diagnosis plus diagnosis=unattributed|env, matching the worker's implementation.

objections.body: interface_contracts.dispatch says `ticket.attempt.start` carries kv kind=diagnosis, but `event.py emit … --kv kind=diagnosis` crashes (measured: `TypeError: emit() got multiple values for argument 'kind'`), and the row's `kind` key is the event kind itself — the kv needs another key (e.g. attempt_kind) or event.py must change; the case only requires the value `diagnosis` on round 2's start row.
